item.title: First thoughts after watching Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 23 (season 2, episode 11)
item.description:
This post includes a spoiler.

I watched Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 23 twice. 9/10. Story was 5/5, animation was 5/5, voices and audio were 4/5. This was a great episode. The main thing was the battle between Zeo and Elfie.

This episode showed how fierce the battle was between two Magia Vanders. And obviously, Ellenor lost to Elfie with ice magic alone, so they both seemed strong. So, the battle was basically one between the cream of the crop and it was worth watching. Zeo's attacks were mostly simple. He used his lightning to move blazing fast, but that was so fast that the animation got good. Like when he threw the wand and then he instantly reached the place where the wand landed, or when the wand came and broke Elfie's clone from an unexpected angle.

Elfie's magic was the exact opposite. She built an ice castle, made a lot of clones, attacked with hundreds of ice shards from every angle, and summoned more ice by drawing a large magic circle. And also, using those remnants, she completely froze his lightning with her ice magic. What was unexpected was that she punched him, with a perfect, anime-style motion, unlike what I imagine a mage would do, and with her magic, the blow landed on him completely. Also, before starting the incantation of her prime magic, she sat on the handrail of the staircase and slid down, and that was so weird. It probably showed her princess-ish behavior but not something you do during a fight.

The animation itself was also great. It wasn't the kind of episode that stops to talk. Characters, buildings, and objects move a lot and fast in most scenes. Of course, when they talked about something, it stopped, but that made a good contrast with the fast-moving scenes. And the entire episode was for this battle alone, and it didn't even end within the episode. The battle between Will and Devander was more like a showcase of Will's Wis ability, so there was some of that, but not at this level. So I was satisfied with this episode.

Story-wise, Elfie put all her effort into fighting him for Will. It was because she had only waited for Will all along, and it was Elfie's turn to do something. This was great, because I thought she hadn't really done much so far and they already had a relationship. Well, it was still a question why they did, but at least, the fact that she stepped up to fight Zeo with all her might changed my opinion about her in this episode. Colette got angry, though. I guess she's already completely lost her chance.

It was also great how Carriot and Ellenor thought and saw the battle. They knew who those two were, so they didn't stop them. And they also noticed that even Zeo got serious once they both used their prime magic. Finn was also smiling and watching the battle, and somehow he knew everything, including Elfie's secret magic. I wonder why he knew how deep Zeo went into the Dungeon, though. He might've been with Zeo? He used to be with the Mage Queen in the past, so I guess he also enjoyed watching mages' battles.

Also, I liked the voice acting of Elfie before the fight started, and Sarissa's shout was great too.

So what's going to happen in the next episode? It looks like Aaron will come down into the venue and butt in. Then Will is going to join Elfie's faction and the season will end shortly.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 22 (season 2, episode 10)
item.description:
This post includes a spoiler.

I watched Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 22 twice. 7/10. Story was 4/5, animation was 3/5, voices and audio were 3/5.

I was wondering who Cerridwen was. It sounded like Caldron, and now here she was — she was surely Cerridwen. I should've been more confident that it was her, and it made sense that she put in the effort to make Will climb the tower. Because otherwise, it was irresponsible that she just chose him over others' objections to make him climb, and he ended up being a guinea pig. Although, she had so much free time that she didn't have to work as the head of the academy lol But now, it was the opposite. Cerridwen was her true form, and Caldron was a disguise she kept up with aging magic.

She couldn't figure out how to make Will grow stronger for 6 years, but I guess she was finally able to figure something out. Or maybe she could've done it at any time, and it was just that Will had lost his memory and his hair color. So the time had finally come for him.

Also about Finn. It made sense why he handed Will over to Cerridwen now because she had a plan, but then why and how was he there? Did he have that much free time? Well, maybe he did. At least he'd lived for 500 years. He had nothing to do but try to grow the "sword" for him. And he didn't save Will at all even when Zeo attacked him.

In this episode, Will used his Wis from the start. This was the moment he grew stronger again. In the praxis, he got stronger with Wis, and the next step was this time, to use Wis through his own power. What was nonsense was that other people talked up his sword's strength against the Wors Ooze. That thing could be killed with even a tiny amount of magic. Other than Zeo, I felt they exaggerated.

And I was glad to see Colette. She was trying to help Will, and was also jealous of Elfie. Although, she couldn't do anything in the Bloom, so I wanted a scene where she got to do something for Will. Maybe Elfie, who took Will for granted, wasn't someone I liked? I don't know. Well, but her role, and Sion's, Julius's, Lihanna's, and Wignall's. Were they just there to explain what was happening around Will? He was away from them the whole time, too.

Kreutz was simply nonsense in this episode.

Now I realized, I liked the ending a lot. "Reach for the Light," I guess. I am still wondering what that scene with Colette as a child was about, but maybe that scene was not included in season 2.

item.title: First thoughts after watching Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 21 (season 2, episode 9)
item.description:
This post includes a spoiler.

I watched Wistoria: Wand and Sword episode 21 twice. 7/10. Story was 4/5, animation was 4/5, voices and audio were 3/5. Well, this episode was about one day in Will's past. And he slept almost an entire day until the next Bloom.

It was a good episode in that it showed Elfie being saved by Will, and that was one reason she loves him. But even before that, she liked him a lot for some reason. There might be more episodes about Elfie and Will in the future.

Will's Wis power was still unknown, but Cerridwen mentioned a few things. From what she said, it sounded like his body drained most of the magic surrounding him, and that explained why he couldn't use magic. And also he had a similar power to "One For All", so it was exciting that the mage queen, who is somehow related to his power, sealed it inside him so he couldn't use it. I also wondered why he couldn't use his power by himself in season 1 or in Terminalia. But he never took huge damage — he just got disappointed. Because Will forgot a lot of things, maybe his power is related, and it's not only magic but also memories that get lost?

There was a photo of Elfie and Will as kids at the end, in the Single Witch's manor, so Cerridwen might be the person who took care of them in their orphanage. But that picture was drawn while he was asleep, so maybe it was from his recollection?

In terms of animation, it really looked like a dream world at first when Will was in his memory, like a world in a drawing. It might have been a scene from a time he enjoyed spending with her. The colors were a little unusual, and mainly greenish or bluish. But before fighting the monster, the art style went back to normal. Also, when Will held the sword and tried to push back against the monster, Elfie jumped onto the sword and spun around the handle. It was funny to look at because her jumping on and grabbing the handle didn't change the speed or anything between the monster's push and Will's resistance.
